title: Perf sim: true server-side cancellation of superseded HOT2000 runs
description:
Backend rework to support the 'latest-wins / supersede' model for the Performance tab (option #2 from the auto-run design discussion).

PROBLEM: The Performance tab will auto-run HOT2000 on input change (debounced, latest-wins). Option #1 (frontend collapse-to-latest + AbortController) lets a stale in-flight run finish before the newest starts (head-of-line blocking): the single worker runs HOT2000 to completion, and the client abort only hides the stale RESULT -- it does not free the worker. This bead removes that wasted tail by terminating the in-flight run when a newer request supersedes it, so the latest inputs start computing immediately.

SCOPE:
- Replace subprocess.run in server/src/perf_server/sim_harness.py with Popen + a cancellation token; terminate()/kill() the HOT2000.exe process on supersession.
- Replace the asyncio.Lock queue (perf_server/queue.py) with a 'current job + supersede' model: a new request cancels the running one rather than queuing behind it.
- Give each run its own isolated working subdir under the CLI install (not the shared sim-harness-work) and clean it up on cancel -- killing mid-run leaves HOT2000 scratch files (contamination observed during Task B0; see server/COMPLIANCE_NOTES.md).
- Handle the cancelled-run case cleanly (do not surface a 500 for an intentionally-cancelled run).

DEPENDS ON: the auto-run/supersede Performance-tab design (option #1) landing first. Only build this if option #1's wasted-tail latency actually feels sluggish -- runs measured ~2-4s on Ryan's machine during B0, so the penalty may be tolerable without it.

NOTE: latest-wins is per-session; a shared single HOT2000 worker still contends across concurrent users -- relevant only if/when public deployment (open legal question) is resolved.
